page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average to strong tiers. It demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2078.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 33.17 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is solid, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 16818.07 and a Passmark CPU score of 27549.65. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which support workloads like low-latency LLM inference. For example, text generation using a small 135M model reaches a strong 267.15 tokens/sec, while a medium 7B model processes text generation at 13.14 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i-flex.4xlarge utilizes a flex-performance model designed to deliver a balance of compute, memory, and network resources for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of fully dedicated, non-flex instances. However, users should note the baseline network bandwidth is limited to 3 Gbps, and there is no local NVMe storage included, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external network-attached volumes.

This instance is suited for general-purpose applications, including web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate machine learning inference. Its balanced resource profile supports Redis key-value stores, executing approximately 22.06 million SET operations per second, and static web serving at 27.93 GB/sec.
